sources.author: Harrison Chase
sources.headline: Co-founder & CEO at LangChain
sources.post_summary: Discussed the rapid evolution of AI agents from simple chains to autonomous systems capable of multi-step reasoning and tool use. Highlighted how developer tooling around memory, planning, and evaluation is becoming critical infrastructure for production agents.

sources.author: Simon Willison
sources.headline: Independent AI researcher & creator of Datasette
sources.post_summary: Shared insights on building reliable AI infrastructure for agents, emphasizing the need for better observability, testing frameworks, and cost controls. Warned against overhyping agent capabilities without robust backend systems.

sources.author: Santiago Valdarrama
sources.headline: AI Engineer & Educator
sources.post_summary: Explored practical patterns for deploying AI agents in production environments, including orchestration with tools like CrewAI and AutoGen. Stressed the importance of human-in-the-loop automation to reduce hallucination risks.

sources.author: Swyx
sources.headline: Founder at Latent Space & AI Engineer
sources.post_summary: Analyzed the emerging stack for AI developer tools, covering vector databases, agent frameworks, and evaluation platforms. Predicted consolidation around a few key infrastructure players in the next 12 months.

sources.author: Alex Hormozi
sources.headline: Founder @ Acquisition.com | Author of $100M Offers
sources.post_summary: Discussed how outbound automation combined with content strategy can scale lead gen without increasing headcount. Emphasized building systems that compound over time rather than one-off campaigns.

sources.author: Elena Verna
sources.headline: Growth Advisor | Ex-Notion, Amplitude, SurveyMonkey
sources.post_summary: Shared a framework for aligning product-led growth with outbound motions. Highlighted how sales ops and revenue operations teams should co-own GTM engineering to reduce friction in the buyer journey.

sources.author: Harry Stebbings
sources.headline: Founder @ 20VC | Investor
sources.post_summary: Posted about the rise of GTM engineering roles and how startups are hiring operators who blend sales ops, automation, and content to drive pipeline. Shared examples from recent portfolio companies.

sources.author: April Dunford
sources.headline: Positioning Expert | Author of Obviously Awesome
sources.post_summary: Explained how content strategy should be engineered into the GTM process from day one. Argued that revenue operations teams need to treat content as infrastructure, not just marketing support.

sources.author: Kyle Poyar
sources.headline: Operating Partner @ OpenView | SaaS Metrics Expert
sources.post_summary: Broke down metrics for measuring outbound automation effectiveness and how sales ops leaders can use them to optimize revenue operations. Included benchmarks from top-performing SaaS companies.

sources.author: Alex Finn
sources.headline: Solo Founder @ Finny | Ex-Google
sources.post_summary: Shared his journey building Finny, a personal finance tool, as a solo founder. Detailed the first 3 months of development, early user acquisition through Twitter threads, and how he validated the idea with 50 beta users before launching publicly.

sources.author: Priya Sharma
sources.headline: Founder & Engineer @ Notion Templates Co
sources.post_summary: Wrote about pivoting from marketing to full-time indie development. Explained how she shipped her first Notion template product in 6 weeks while working a full-time job and reached $2k MRR within 3 months of launch.

sources.author: Marcus Chen
sources.headline: Building DevTools in Public | Ex-Meta
sources.post_summary: Posted a transparent update on his open-source CLI tool for developers. Shared weekly metrics including 1.2k GitHub stars gained, challenges with documentation, and lessons from handling his first 50 issues from the community.

sources.author: Elena Rodriguez
sources.headline: Solo Developer | Career Switcher from Teaching
sources.post_summary: Detailed her transition from high school teacher to shipping her first SaaS product, a lesson planning tool. Covered learning to code via bootcamp, the 8-month build process, and securing her first 20 paying customers through educator communities.
